title: Singleton extension is K-flat on the whole sequence site
statement: Let C be an essentially small site in coefficient universe w, B an inverse sequence of commutative ring sheaves, S a normalized scalar assignment, and T its tensor coherence. Use the fixed ordinary singleton E_n on the ringed sequence site [def-pur-system-singleton-scalar-comparisons]. For every unbounded flat-term K-flat B_n-complex P [def-pc-kflat-complex], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], its termwise singleton E_n(P) is K-flat and has flat terms on the whole ringed sequence site, with its actual sequence-site tensor, not only componentwise K-flatness.

source.place: Parent Steps 4--5: Stacks 06YN and 0G7E; Zheng Construction 4.1.

proof.text: Vertical covers compute sheafification and module tensor at each fixed level. Below n the singleton term is scalar extension along B_n → B_j, hence flat by flat-module pullback; above n it is zero. Tensoring a short exact sequence stays exact at each level, and the jointly conservative exact evaluations detect this exactness. Thus each term is flat on the whole sequence site.

Let K be an acyclic sequence complex. Evaluation commutes with the coproducts in total tensor. For j ≤ n balancing identifies e_j(K tensor E_n(P)) with Res_{B_n→B_j}(K_j) tensor P, as abelian complexes: x tensor (b tensor p) maps to bx tensor p; the inverse inserts 1. Balancing proves the inverse laws and degree-zero scalar multiplication respects signed differentials. Restriction is exact and P is K-flat, so these evaluated tensors are acyclic. Above n they are zero. Joint detection of cohomology proves acyclicity on the sequence site, which is the K-flat condition.

theorem singletonSequenceOrdinary_kFlat (n : ℕ)
    (P : CochainComplex (systemLevel B n) ℤ) (hP : systemLevelKFlat B n P) :
    CochainComplex.IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients (R := systemSequenceRing B)
      (((singletonSequenceOrdinary S T B n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) ∧
    (∀ i : ℤ, IsFlatOnSite (R := systemSequenceRing B)
      ((singletonSequenceOrdinary S T B n).obj (P.X i)))
